guards: a `process.exit()` that a stdout write can reach must go through `finishAndExit`, which drains stdout first; the population of un-drained sites may not grow

gates.stated: An exit that stdout can reach must drain first

poisonPill.why: The real baseline with 12 site identities removed — the tree as it would look if twelve new un-drained exits had just landed. Not hypothetical: a detector-first census on 2026-09-04 found 190 reachable sites across ~100 files, 95 of them carrying a JSON envelope a caller parses. `finishAndExit`'s own docstring names the failure as observed rather than theoretical: on Windows a piped `process.stdout` is asynchronous, so `process.exit()` discards whatever has not flushed. A truncated envelope surfaces as a SyntaxError attributed to whatever the caller was doing, or — when the cut lands on a complete-looking prefix — a silently short result. What makes this worth pilling is that the defect is invisible everywhere it is written: `process.stdout.write(report); process.exit(0)` is the obvious shape, reads as correct, passes review, and works on Linux and on a terminal. Only the pipe truncates. The gate also fails on a REDUCTION, deliberately: a fixed site belongs in the baseline diff, not silently pocketed at the old high-water mark.
